title: Repository conventions
text: Name argument-validation helpers checkmate, behavior predictable prefix: assert_*(x, ...) – errors x invalid; otherwise returns x (usually invisibly). Use inside function enforce contract, e.g. assert_positive_int(chains, "chains"). check_*(x, ...) – returns TRUE valid, otherwise string describing problem. Reserve check_ prefix TRUE--message shape. test_*(x, ...) – returns single TRUE/FALSE. Use plain yes/predicate, e.g. test_threaded(stan_opts). adding helper, match prefix return contract: predicate answers yes/test_*, check_*.

title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: fit can use cores two ways : Across chains. MCMC chains independent, run parallel near-linear speedup coordination overhead. Within chain (threading). Stan model sums conditionally-independent term reduce_sum() (map_rect), chain can split sum across threads. stan_options(threading = TRUE) looks cores process allowed use, fills chain-parallelism first (“free” – threading overhead), gives leftover cores threads, writes result onto options, tells chose: split, given pool cores divide (pool machine’s cores, max_cores): threading “switches ” pool cores chains – otherwise every core spent running chains. default uses cores, 8-core machine running 4 chains splits pool 8 (4 chains, 2 threads ). fit usual; fit_model() applies allocation whichever backend (, cmdstanr, compiles model threading enabled):
code: opts <- stan_options(chains = 4, threading = TRUE) #> flexstanr: threading enabled. Using 16 of 16 available cores: 4 chains in #> parallel, 4 threads per chain. Pass max_cores to leave some cores free. fit <- fit_model("my_model", dat_stan = dat, init = init, stan_opts = opts)

title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: default threading = TRUE uses available cores. machine becomes unresponsive fit, cap max_cores (e.g. max_cores = 4): threading = FALSE (default) leaves parallelism untouched, can still set cores (rstan) parallel_chains / threads_per_chain (cmdstanr) hand want full manual control.
code: # use at most 4 cores, however many the machine has stan_options(chains = 4, threading = TRUE, max_cores = 4)

what: Model authors: warn when threads can’t be used
title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: Threading helps model actually uses reduce_sum()/map_rect compiled threading. flexstanr know model – write fit function top flexstanr, check whether caller asked threads warn model can’t use . test_threaded() reports options request: keeps division labor clean: user just says threading = TRUE, model author – one knows whether model can thread – tips won’t take effect.
code: run_my_fit <- function(dat_stan, init, stan_opts = stan_options()) {   if (test_threaded(stan_opts) && !model_is_threaded) {     warning(       "threads were requested but this model does not use reduce_sum(); ",       "it will run one thread per chain. Run more chains, use the threaded ",       "model variant, or set threading = FALSE.",       call. = FALSE     )   }   fit_model("my_model", dat_stan = dat_stan, init = init, stan_opts = stan_opts) }

title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: parallel::detectCores() reports every core compute node (often 64, 128+) regardless job’s allocation. fit sizing launch dozens threads inside job pinned handful cores; scheduler’s cgroup throttle crawl. threading = TRUE uses parallelly::availableCores(), reads allocation instead.

what: Single node: let flexstanr split your allocation
title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: Request one task several CPUs let threading = TRUE divide . 4 chains x 2 threads (8 cores):
code: #!/bin/bash #SBATCH --job-name=stan-fit #SBATCH --nodes=1 #SBATCH --ntasks=1 #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8      # availableCores() will report 8 #SBATCH --mem=16G #SBATCH --time=04:00:00 Rscript fit.R # fit.R -- no core arithmetic; availableCores() picks up SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK = 8 opts <- stan_options(chains = 4, iter = 2000, threading = TRUE) fit  <- fit_model("my_model", dat_stan = dat, init = init, stan_opts = opts) saveRDS(fit, "fit.rds")

what: Many chains across nodes: one chain per array task
title: Parallel and threaded fitting (including HPC)
text: Chain-parallelism threads shared-memory: span nodes. scale beyond single node, run one chain per job SLURM array, give job cores threading, combine single-chain fits . stan_options() otherwise sampler explores (iter, warmup, seed, control = list(adapt_delta = ...), …); threading one knob reaches machine.
code: #SBATCH --array=1-4            # one task per chain #SBATCH --nodes=1 #SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8      # all 8 cores -> threads for this one chain i    <- Sys.getenv("SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID") opts <- stan_options(chains = 1, seed = as.integer(i), threading = TRUE) fit  <- fit_model("my_model", dat_stan = dat, init = init, stan_opts = opts) saveRDS(fit, sprintf("chain-%s.rds", i))

text: Decides many chains run parallel many threads chain gets. Chain-parallelism threading overhead scales ~linearly, filled first; leftover cores become per-chain threads: parallel_chains = min(chains, cores) threads_per_chain = max(1L, cores %/% parallel_chains). Cores divide evenly left idle rather rebalanced.

title: flexstanr 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-07-17 Initial release: portable Stan-backend layer Stan-based R package can fit models , using either rstan (default) , optionally, cmdstanr. stan_options() collects validates sampler options chosen backend, forwarding verbatim guarding mixing one backend’s argument vocabulary . fit_model() dispatches fit backend recorded options resolves calling package’s compiled model automatically. Backend-agnostic accessors read fit without knowing backend produced : backend_draws_array(), backend_extract(), backend_generate_quantities(), backend_has_draws(). use_flexstanr() wires flexstanr host package’s DESCRIPTION. cmdstanr optional backend, used requireNamespace() guards; rstan default hard Stan dependency.
